questions.q: What are the three primary methods by which thermal energy can be transferred from one place to another?
How does thermal conduction primarily occur in solid non-metals (insulators)?
a: By bulk movement of fluid particles
By lattice vibrations (phonon transfer) passing atomic kinetic energy from particle to neighboring particle
By emission of infrared light waves

questions.q: Why are metals exceptionally good thermal conductors compared to wood or plastics?
a: Metals contain free delocalized electrons that can move rapidly through the crystal lattice, transferring kinetic energy quickly throughout the material.

questions.q: What is convection?
a: The transfer of heat through a vacuum by electromagnetic waves
The direct transfer of vibration between adjacent stationary atoms
The flow of electric charge through a metal wire
The transfer of thermal energy through fluids (liquids and gases) by the bulk movement of warmer, less dense regions rising and cooler, denser regions sinking

questions.q: Why does a convection current form when a beaker of water is heated from the bottom?
a: Water at the bottom expands when heated, becomes less dense, and rises, while cooler, denser water sinks to take its place.
Water molecules become magnetic when warm.
Glass walls push water in circles.

questions.q: What type of electromagnetic wave is primarily responsible for thermal radiation (infrared radiation)?
Which type of surface is the best absorber and best emitter of infrared thermal radiation?
Why are solar water heaters painted with a matt black coating on their absorbing panels?
a: To maximize the absorption of incident infrared thermal radiation from the Sun

questions.q: How does a vacuum flask (Thermos flask) minimize heat transfer by conduction?
a: By using a double-walled glass container with a vacuum between the walls, since conduction requires a medium of particles to travel through
By filling the gap with dense water

questions.q: How does a vacuum flask minimize heat transfer by convection?
a: By eliminating gas particles in the vacuum gap, preventing fluid bulk movement and convection currents

questions.q: How does a vacuum flask minimize heat transfer by radiation?
a: By using a thick rubber stopper
By silvering the internal glass surfaces to reflect infrared radiation back toward the contents

questions.q: Why do double-glazed windows provide better thermal insulation for houses than single-pane glass windows?
a: They trap a layer of dry air or gas between two glass panes, significantly reducing thermal conduction and convection heat loss.

questions.q: In a domestic hot water system, why is the heating element or boiler usually placed at the bottom of the water tank?
a: To set up a convection current that heats the entire volume of water efficiently from bottom to top

questions.q: Why do land breezes occur near coastal areas during nighttime?
a: The land retains heat longer than the sea.
The sea stays warmer than the land during the night, causing warm air above the sea to rise and cooler air from the land to blow out toward the sea.
Sunlight heats the sand at night.
Wind travels from high altitude to low altitude.

questions.q: Which of the following materials is commonly used in roof loft insulation to trap air and reduce heat loss from a building?
How does wearing layers of woolen clothing keep a person warm in cold weather?
a: Wool conducts heat rapidly away from the body.
Wool traps pockets of trapped air, which is a poor thermal conductor, preventing rapid heat loss from the body.

questions.q: If you touch a piece of metal and a piece of wood in a room that is at 20 degrees Celsius, why does the metal feel much colder to the touch than the wood?
a: Metal is a good thermal conductor and rapidly conducts heat away from your warm fingers, whereas wood is a poor conductor (insulator).
Metal is at a lower temperature than wood.

questions.q: Why are cavity walls in modern houses often filled with foam insulation or mineral wool?
a: To trap air pockets in tiny cavities, preventing convection currents and reducing thermal conduction through the wall
To stop sound waves from entering
To prevent water pipes from freezing outside

questions.q: Unlike conduction and convection, how does thermal radiation travel through space?
a: As electromagnetic waves that do not require any medium or particles

questions.q: Why do firefighters wear reflective silver-coated suits when approaching intense fires?
a: To reflect radiant heat away and protect them from severe thermal radiation burns

questions.q: Why are saucepan bases often made of thick copper or aluminum, while their handles are made of plastic or wood?
a: Metals conduct heat rapidly to the food inside, while plastic handles are poor conductors so they stay cool enough to touch safely without burns.
Copper reflects heat away from food.
Wood conducts heat faster than metal.

questions.q: What happens to the rate of thermal radiation emitted by an object when its temperature is increased?
a: Emission rate increases significantly, and the emitted wavelength spectrum shifts to shorter wavelengths.
The object turns into a liquid.

questions.q: Why do penguins huddling together in freezing Antarctic conditions survive severe cold?
a: They minimize their exposed surface area to volume ratio, reducing overall heat loss by radiation and convection.

questions.q: What is the main reason why chimneys are built tall above houses with open fireplaces?
a: To block wind from entering the room
To establish a strong upward convection current of hot combustion gases, drawing fresh air into the fire

questions.q: Which of the following surfaces is the worst emitter of infrared radiation?
a: Polished silver or shiny chrome surface

questions.q: How does heat reach the Earth from the Sun across the vacuum of space?
a: By infrared radiation traveling as electromagnetic waves
By convection currents in the upper atmosphere

questions.q: Why are domestic radiators usually placed underneath windows in living rooms?
a: To set up a vertical convection current that warms cold air descending from the window, circulating heat evenly around the room

questions.q: Why are car engines often surrounded by cooling fins made of metal?
a: To increase the surface area of metal, maximizing heat dissipation by conduction, convection, and radiation to prevent overheating

questions.q: Which state of matter cannot transfer thermal energy via convection currents, and why?
a: Solids, because their particles are held in fixed positions and cannot undergo bulk movement
Gases, because they have no mass
Liquids, because they have zero thermal energy
Plasma, because it is too hot

questions.q: What is the purpose of painting domestic water storage tanks in a loft with bright white or shiny reflective paint?
a: To minimize heat absorption from the surroundings by radiation
To make them easier to see in the dark

questions.q: A sealed metal container of hot water cools down faster when its outer surface is painted matt black compared to when it is polished silver. Why?
a: Black paint makes the water colder inside.
Silver paint absorbs heat from the air.
Matt black surfaces are much better emitters of infrared thermal radiation.
Black paint increases the mass of the container.

questions.q: Why do double-glazed window manufacturers sometimes evacuate the air completely between the two glass panes or fill the gap with argon gas?
a: To inflate the window like a balloon
To eliminate air convection currents and reduce thermal conduction further than standard air

questions.q: What is the primary method of heat transfer through a concrete house floor resting directly on the ground?
Why do tropical houses often have white or light-colored exterior walls and roofs?
a: To absorb heat during the night
To reflect incident solar radiation and keep the interior cooler

questions.q: How does a ceiling fan cool a room down by circulating air?
a: By increasing air speed across human skin, which enhances sweat evaporation and convective cooling

questions.q: Which of the following materials has the lowest thermal conductivity?
When boiling soup in a metal pot, heat travels through the metal base primarily by what process?
Why are freezer compartments in domestic refrigerators positioned at the top of the fridge cabinet rather than the bottom?
a: To make food easier to reach
Cold air is denser than warm air, so it sinks from the top, setting up a convection current that cools the entire refrigerator cabinet efficiently

questions.q: Which form of thermal energy transfer requires physical contact between objects of different temperatures?
Why does an Eskimo igloo made of compressed snow blocks provide effective thermal insulation against freezing external arctic winds?
a: Snow is made of solid ice crystals which conduct heat very well.
Snow blocks are heated by electricity.
Packed snow contains numerous tiny trapped air pockets, making it an excellent thermal insulator that retains body heat.
